newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican insured workers up 7.8 pct in '96 - report.
newsitem.headline: Mexican insured workers up 7.8 pct in '96 - report.

text.p: The number of workers insured in the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) grew 7.8 percent in 1996 compared with the end of 1995, Reforma newspaper reported on Friday, citing IMSS figures.
It said the number of insured workers rose to 9.164 million in December 1996 compared with 8.502 million at the end of the previous year.
It described the 662,000 new IMSS members in 1996 as the highest one-year rate of affiliation in history.
Of the total IMSS membership, 40 percent worked in the industrial sector, 36.2 percent in services, 19.4 percent in commerce, and 4.6 percent in the agricultural sector.

Some 57 percent of jobs created in 1996 were in industry and 25.3 percent were in services. Reforma said most jobs in the commercial sector were created in the buying and selling of raw materials, as well as supermarkets and groceries.
The agricultural sector only added some 16,000 workers to IMSS payrolls, it said.
